Subject: Data usage exclusions & subprocessor evidence (onboarding)

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — team was impressed. Before we can onboard, our legal and procurement teams need a short set of confirmations around data usage and subprocessors. High level ask below: 

- Confirmation that HealthEdge production data will not be used to improve models (no-training/no-derive) unless we opt-in in writing.
- Concrete evidence you can provide: a one-page attestation letter for our procurement file; current subprocessor inventory and the last annual attestation for those subprocessors; SOC2 report or equivalent; any residency/export constraints.
- Any mandatory cross-border transfer scenarios and where data could be processed (US only vs multi-region).

Could you put together what you can share + a proposed timeline for the attestation? Procurement is cc'd on this thread (purchasing@healthedge.com).

Best,
Samantha Gupta
Head of Product Security
HealthEdge Labs

Hi Samantha — great to hear the demo landed well. Short answers up front, and then a proposed next step roadmap: 

- No-training: Redwood offers a contractual no-training / model-improvement exclusion for customer-provided content. We can commit in the DPA and provide an attestation letter scoped to HealthEdge once procurement confirms the exact contract form.
- Ownership: Customer prompts & responses remain your data — we do not assert ownership over your outputs. We can reference explicit language in the DPA redline.
- Subprocessors: we maintain an inventory and annual attestations; I can share the current csv and a redline of the DPA with relevant clauses.
- Transfers/residency: Hosted infrastructure primarily processes in the US by default; we have EU regions for customers who require EU-only processing. If you require an EU residency commitment, that will be an addendum.

Proposed timeline:
1) I'll loop in Monica (legal/CS) — she can share the redline and subprocessor inventory (today).
2) Monica to draft the one-page attestation we can sign (1-3 business days).
3) Procurement/Legal review + DocuSign (dependent on your timelines).

If that works I'll send the initial DPA redline and subprocessor export now.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Cell: +1 (415) 555-0198

Hi Samantha — looping in Aditya from our privacy team as well. Attached please find: 

- redwood_dpa_v2_redline.pdf (PDF, 142KB) — the DPA with a proposed no-training clause (see §3.4) and a prompt/response ownership paragraph.
- subprocessor_inventory_202508.csv (CSV, 18KB) — current subprocessors and processing jurisdictions.

Quick notes on the language we proposed (high level):
- No-train/no-derive: We added a short clause that explicitly prohibits using HealthEdge customer-provided content to train or improve any model, including derivative datasets, unless you provide written opt-in. The clause includes standard carveouts for telemetry/ops metrics (aggregate, de-identified only).
- Subprocessor attestations: We can provide last-attested dates and redacted attestations for third parties that hold customer data. For customers needing complete audit packs, we can arrange a scoped review under an NDA.
- Data residency: If HealthEdge needs EU-only processing, we recommend the Private deployment option (VPC). Hosted EU regions are available but we can't guarantee full data residency for some peripheral tooling without the Private contract addendum.

Next steps: please confirm whether the one-page attestation will suffice for procurement. If so, Aditya will prepare the attestation and include the exact wording we will sign. If you need anything formalized differently (e.g., signed addendum vs attestation letter), let us know so we can route to Legal.

2) For subprocessor attestations we need either: (a) the last attestation emails from those subprocessors explicitly referencing HealthEdge data, or (b) a single attestation from Redwood confirming you have requested & retained attestation documentation (redacted is ok). Which is easier for you?
3) On residency: HealthEdge is aiming for US-only for now. Are there any subprocessors in the inventory that would necessitate EU/other transfers for primary data processing? If yes, we need to know which ones and whether Private deployment is required.

Procurement is copy — Amit Sharma (amit.sharma@healthedge.com) will own PO and DocuSign. Can you provide the attestation and a short note on subprocessor feasibility by end of week?

Samantha
